items.question: How should one bound by bonds be presented to the goddess?
premises: the bound one is in genitive relation
items.inference: The verse frames the bound practitioner as an offering or object of address to the goddess.
items.plain_english: O goddess, of one bound by bonds.

items.question: By what fortunes should this practitioner be increased?
premises: increase is requested for this person
items.inference: The practitioner should prosper in both worldly and otherworldly respects.
items.plain_english: May this one be increased by worldly and otherworldly fortunes.

rows.grounds: locative singular masculine or neuter adjective

items.question: Where is the mantra joined with rishi and others to be placed?
premises: the mantra is joined with rishi and others
items.inference: The mantra is to be placed in the right ear.
uncertainties: whether śravasi is strictly ear or hearing
items.plain_english: The mantra joined with rishi and others is in the right ear.

items.question: Who are the authorities across all tantras in this context?
items.inference: The verse identifies mantra-knowers and tantra-knowers as the relevant authorities.
uncertainties: exact syntactic role of the instrumental agents
items.plain_english: In all tantras, by mantra-knowers and tantra-knowers.

items.question: What qualities must the disciple have before receiving instruction?
items.inference: The disciple must abandon deceit about wealth and remain contented.
uncertainties: whether vittaśāṭhya means stinginess or deceit
items.plain_english: The disciple, abandoning wealth-deceit, has a contented mind.

rows.grounds: fused compound of yathā-śaktyā and atha-vā

items.question: What are the permitted alternatives for the wise one's offering?
premises: half of that is one option
the wise one is the subject
items.inference: The wise one may give half or as much as he is able.
items.plain_english: Half of that, or as able, the wise one.

items.question: Which text is cited in the Dakshinamurti tantra?
items.inference: The verse cites the Gargya samhita within the Dakshinamurti tantra.
uncertainties: whether śrī modifies the samhita or is a separate token
items.plain_english: In the Dakshinamurti tantra, the Shri Gargya samhita.

rows.grounds: fused sandhi of phalam and yataḥ

items.question: Why are the two said to be useless in relation to the Vedic rite?
premises: the complete Vedic rite is the source
items.inference: The verse attributes their uselessness to fruit in relation to the complete Vedic rite.
items.plain_english: The two are useless from the complete Vedic rite because of fruit.

items.question: For what purpose does the wise mantra-practitioner recite?
premises: the wise one is the subject
items.inference: The wise mantra-practitioner recites for accomplishment of the mantra's meaning.
uncertainties: whether budho and mantrī are appositional
items.plain_english: The wise mantra-practitioner, having recited, for mantra-meaning accomplishment.

items.question: What obligations follow the mantra practice regarding brahmins?
items.inference: The practitioner should give dakshina and feed brahmins.
uncertainties: whether api modifies brahmins or the whole clause
items.plain_english: He should give dakshina and also feed brahmins.

items.question: What is the state of the initiated disciple?
items.inference: The initiated disciple has diminished impurity.
uncertainties: whether kṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ is result or description
items.plain_english: The initiated disciple, with diminished impurity.

items.question: What kind of attachment is described for the given mantra?
premises: it belongs to the given mantra's practitioner
items.inference: The verse describes a clinging attachment to the mantra given to its practitioner.
items.plain_english: The mantra-attachment that clings to the given mantra's practitioner.
